claim.why_it_matters: Two lines of Annex E.3.2 normative-looking text (the new-exception-condition lists for Asynchronous messaging and for Commit and Rollback) are appended to the back cover, where the PDF prints nothing at all. The block is also truncated: its parent lead-in '— For the Asynchronous messaging facility' was dropped, so the first line begins with a bare ' (EC-MCS, ...' with no antecedent. The legitimate copy of both lines already exists at its true home, specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 48920 and 48922, under '3) Exception conditions. New exception conditions have been added:' on page 1211. So this is a duplicated orphan, not lost text — but a reader or a tool that greps for EC-MCS-* / EC-FLOW-* gets a second hit anchored to page 1261, attributing annex content to the back cover and inviting a bogus '§ on page 1261' citation.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED on every element, by independent render and by reading the markdown source. (1) PDF page 1261 (rendered at 300 dpi to E:/Temp/specrecon/v1261/spec_p1261.png, 2550x3300) is the back cover and is empty apart from five furniture bands. A per-row ink scan (pixels < 160 grey) finds inked rows ONLY at y=48-93 (running head 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023(E)'), y=3030-3044 (the triple horizontal rule), y=3093-3127 ('ICS  35.060'), y=3161-3194 ('Price based on 1229 pages'), and y=3246-3295 ('© ISO/IEC 2023 - All rights reserved' overprinted by the '[per-copy licence stamp]' watermark). Rows 94 through 3029 - the entire body of the page - contain zero dark pixels. There is no EC-MCS or EC-FLOW text anywhere on the printed page. (2) The markdown DOES carry the extra block: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 53199 and 53201, inside the '## Page [1261]' section that opens at line 53189 and runs to end-of-file at line 53204, i.e. the block is the last content in the file with no following page anchor. (3) The truncation is real: line 53199 begins with a leading space and an open parenthesis - ' (EC-MCS, ...' - with no lead-in; the em-dash phrase '— For the Asynchronous messaging facility' that governs it is absent from that location (grep for 'Asynchronous messaging facility' returns exactly one hit in the whole file, at line 48920). (4) The duplication claim is exact: lines 48920 and 48922 carry the complete, correctly-formed pair ('   — For the Asynchronous messaging facility (EC-MCS, ... EC-MCS-REQUESTOR-FAILED)' and '   — For the Commit and Rollback facility (EC-FLOW-APPLY-COMMIT, EC-FLOW-COMMIT and EC-FLOW-ROLLBACK)') under line 48918 '3) **Exception conditions.** New exception conditions have been added:' in §E.3.2, and those lines sit between the page-1211 anchor (line 48886) and the page-1212 anchor (line 48926), so they are indeed on page 1211. Line 53201 is byte-identical to line 48922; line 53199 is line 48920 with its leading '   — For the Asynchronous messaging facility' prefix stripped. No reading of this as reflow, wrapping, hyphenation, or page-break furniture survives: the text is genuinely absent from the PDF page and genuinely present in the markdown section, and it is annex body prose, not running-head or footer matter. Nothing normative is lost, so the defect is a spurious duplicate anchored to the wrong page, exactly as claimed.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as filed; no correction needed. Adding only precise locations for the fix: delete specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 53197-53204 down to the trailing blank lines - specifically the orphan content at line 53199 (' (EC-MCS, EC-MCS-ABNORMAL-TERMINATION, EC-MCS-IMP, EC-MCS-INVALID-TAG, EC-MCS-MESSAGE-LENGTH, EC-MCS-NO-REQUESTOR, EC-MCS-NO-SERVER, EC-MCS-NORMAL-TERMINATION, EC-MCS-REQUESTOR-FAILED)') and line 53201 ('   — For the Commit and Rollback facility (EC-FLOW-APPLY-COMMIT, EC-FLOW-COMMIT and EC-FLOW-ROLLBACK)'), leaving the page-1261 section as just the running head, the rule, '**ICS 35.060**' and 'Price based on 1229 pages'. Do NOT touch lines 48920/48922, which are the correct §E.3.2 originals on page 1211. Two incidental notes, neither a defect: the page-1261 section also omits the '© ISO/IEC 2023 - All rights reserved' footer, consistent with the transcription's convention of dropping footer/watermark furniture throughout; and the orphan block is the physical end of the file, which is consistent with an extraction-pipeline flush of a dangling buffer rather than a mis-assigned page.
